transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brings me in is... I got really worked up in a staff meeting recently. I just started acting out this whole fall-prevention drill right there in the room. I was moving chairs around and waving my arms all over the place, and... I just couldn't seem to stop. Even when folks were telling me to sit down, I just kept going. So, that's why I'm here.
Have you had any other episodes recently where you felt unable to control your actions or behaved in a way that others found unusual?
No, I don't think so. It was just that one time at the staff meeting. I haven't really done anything else like that lately.
Before you started moving the chairs and waving your arms during the meeting, did you feel like you had to do it or that you couldn't stop yourself from acting that way?

I don't know if I felt like I had to do it, exactly. I wasn't really thinking about it like that. It just felt like something I needed to show everyone right then. And once I started doing it, I just kept going. I didn't really stop to think about whether I could control it or not, to be honest.
Before you started moving the chairs and acting out the drill, did you feel a sudden urge or impulse that you couldn't resist?

No, it wasn't really a sudden urge or... an impulse taking over. Like I was saying, I just thought they needed to see it, so I got up and did it. I wasn't fighting against it or feeling like I couldn't resist. It just seemed like the right thing to do at the time, so I just did it.

While you were moving the chairs and acting out the drill, were you fully aware of what you were doing, or did you feel like you were in a different state of mind or not completely in control of your thoughts?

I was aware of what I was doing, yeah. I mean, I knew I was moving chairs and showing them the drill. I didn't feel like I was in a trance or anything like that. I was just focused on making sure they understood what I was trying to show them. I felt like I was in control of my thoughts, it just made sense to me at the time to do it that way.
As you were acting out the drill, did you feel like you were on autopilot or that your actions were happening without you actively controlling them?

I wouldn't really call it autopilot, no. I was doing it on purpose because I just got so worked up about it. I was right in the middle of acting out that whole fall-prevention drill, moving the chairs around and waving my arms to show them how to do it. 

But... I guess the part I didn't have control over was stopping. When folks started telling me to sit down and quit, I just couldn't seem to stop. I heard them, but I just kept right on going with the drill anyway.
While you were acting out the drill, did you feel like reality was different in any way—like things seemed unreal, or you felt detached from yourself or the situation?

No, I didn't feel like that. Everything seemed real to me. I knew exactly where I was and what I was doing. I didn't feel detached or like I was floating outside my body or anything weird like that. I was just right there in the room with everyone else, showing them the drill.

Before you started acting out the drill, did you notice any strange feelings, unusual sensations, or automatic movements that you weren't fully aware of—like chewing motions, lip smacking, or fumbling with your hands?

No, I didn't have anything like that. I wasn't doing any weird chewing or messing with my hands or anything. I was just talking to them, and then I got up to show them the drill. There wasn't any weird feeling before it happened.

Before you started acting out the drill, did you notice any warning signs or strange feelings—like a sensation in your stomach, a strange taste, or a feeling that something wasn’t quite right—just before it happened?

No, nothing like that. My stomach felt fine, and I didn't have any weird tastes or... or any feeling that something was off. I was just talking, getting worked up about the safety stuff, and then I was up and doing it. There wasn't any kind of warning or strange feeling right before.
While you were acting out the drill, did you notice yourself doing anything automatically—like repetitive movements, gestures, or behaviors that you weren't consciously controlling?
No, I wasn't doing anything like that. I was just... I was just showing them the drill. I wasn't doing any weird movements that I couldn't control. I was just acting it out, like I said.
After you finished acting out the drill, did you feel confused, sleepy, or like you couldn't remember what had just happened?

No, I didn't feel confused or sleepy. I remembered everything just fine. I was just... I don't know, maybe a little out of breath from moving around, but I knew exactly what I had just done. I just sat back down after.
After you started acting out the drill, did you notice any point where you weren't fully aware of what you were doing, or did part of your body move on its own without you meaning to?

No, nothing like that. I was fully aware the whole time. I knew I was standing up and moving around, showing them what to do. My body didn't do anything on its own, I was in control of all my movements. I just... I was just demonstrating the safety drill, that's all.
During the episode, were any of your movements completely involuntary—like sudden twitches, jerks, or movements you weren’t trying to do on purpose?

No, I didn't have any twitches or jerks. Like I said, I was just moving on purpose to show them the drill. Everything I did was because I wanted to do it. There weren't any sudden movements or anything I couldn't control.

Did you find yourself doing anything during the episode that felt like it was happening automatically, without you fully meaning to do it, like routine actions or complex movements that you weren't consciously planning as you went along?

No, not really. I wasn't on autopilot or anything like that. I mean, I knew what I was doing the whole time. I was just... I was thinking about showing them the drill, so I did it. It wasn't like my body was just going through the motions without me telling it to. I planned it out in my head as I was doing it.
Before or during the time you were acting out the drill, did you feel anxious, tense, or emotionally upset in any way?

No, I didn't feel anxious or upset at all. I was... I felt completely fine, actually. Just really focused on making sure everyone knew what to do for the drill. There wasn't any tension or anything like that.
After you sat back down following the drill, did you feel confused, disconnected, or as though part of you wasn't fully present for a while?
No, I felt completely normal when I sat back down. I wasn't confused or anything. I just went back to what I was doing before. I was fully there the whole time.
After you sat back down following the drill, did you notice any time where you weren't fully aware of your surroundings or found yourself doing something without realizing you were doing it?
No, not at all. Like I said, I was fully there. I didn't zone out or start doing things without realizing it. I just sat down and went back to normal.

While you were acting out the drill, did you have any moment where your awareness of the situation changed—like feeling spaced out, zoning out, or doing things without being fully aware of why you were doing them?
No, I was fully aware the whole time. I didn't space out or anything like that. I knew exactly what I was doing and why I was doing it. I was just focused on the drill.
